title: Existential completion of a variable prefix
statement: Let $m$ be a CNF formula over variables indexed by the natural numbers, let $j,i\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $\sigma:\mathbb{N}\to\{0,1\}$. If the variable count of $m$ is at most $i+j$, then the formula is true under $j$ successive existential choices for variables $i$ through $i+j-1$, starting from $\sigma$, if and only if there is an assignment $\tau$ agreeing with $\sigma$ on every variable below $i$ such that $m$ evaluates to true under $\tau$.
hypotheses_covered: $m$ is a CNF formula over natural-number variables
$\sigma$ is a Boolean assignment to natural-number variables
The variable count of $m$ is at most $i+j$
